1230	  def detect_shell
1231	    # Check SHELL env (Unix), then parent process, then PSModulePath for PowerShell
1232	    shell_env = ENV["SHELL"].to_s
1233	    return 'fish' if shell_env.include?('fish')
1234	    return 'zsh' if shell_env.include?('zsh')
1235	    return 'bash' if shell_env.include?('bash')
1236	
1237	    # PowerShell detection: PSModulePath is set in pwsh sessions
1238	    return 'pwsh' if ENV["PSModulePath"] && !ENV["PSModulePath"].empty?
1239	
1240	    # Fallback: check parent process name
1241	    parent = (`ps c -p #{Process.ppid} -o 'ucomm='`.strip rescue nil)
1242	    return 'fish' if parent&.include?('fish')
1243	    return 'zsh' if parent&.include?('zsh')
1244	    return 'bash' if parent&.include?('bash')
1245	    return 'pwsh' if parent&.match?(/pwsh|powershell/i)
1246	
1247	    nil
1248	  end
1249	
1250	  def shell_rc_file(shell)
1251	    case shell
1252	    when 'fish' then '~/.config/fish/config.fish'
1253	    when 'zsh'  then '~/.zshrc'
1254	    when 'bash'
1255	      # Prefer .bashrc, fall back to .bash_profile on macOS
1256	      File.exist?(File.expand_path('~/.bashrc')) ? '~/.bashrc' : '~/.bash_profile'
1257	    when 'pwsh'
1258	      # PowerShell profile path from $PROFILE, or the standard location
1259	      ENV["PROFILE"] || (Gem.win_platform? ?
1260	        File.join(ENV["USERPROFILE"] || Dir.home, "Documents", "PowerShell", "Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1") :
1261	        File.join(Dir.home, ".config", "powershell", "Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1"))
1262	    end
1263	  end
1264	
1265	  def init_snippet(shell, script_path, explicit_path, default_path)
1266	    case shell
1267	    when 'fish'
1268	      fish_path_arg = explicit_path ? " --path '#{explicit_path}'" : " --path (if set -q TRY_PATH; echo \"$TRY_PATH\"; else; echo '#{default_path}'; end)"
1269	      <<~FISH
1270	        function try
1271	          set -l out (/usr/bin/env ruby '#{script_path}' exec#{fish_path_arg} $argv 2>/dev/tty | string collect)
1272	          if test $pipestatus[1] -eq 0
1273	            eval $out
1274	          else
1275	            echo $out
1276	          end
1277	        end
1278	      FISH
1279	    when 'pwsh'
1280	      ps_path_expr = if explicit_path
1281	        "'#{explicit_path}'"
1282	      else
1283	        "$(if ($env:TRY_PATH) { $env:TRY_PATH } else { '#{default_path}' })"
1284	      end
1285	      <<~PWSH
1286	        function try {
1287	          $tryPath = #{ps_path_expr}
1288	          $tempErr = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName()
1289	          $out = & ruby '#{script_path}' exec --path $tryPath @args 2>$tempErr
1290	          if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
1291	            $out | Invoke-Expression
1292	          } else {
1293	            Get-Content $tempErr | Write-Host
1294	            $out | Write-Output
1295	          }
1296	          Remove-Item $tempErr -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
1297	        }
1298	      PWSH
1299	    else # bash, zsh
1300	      path_arg = explicit_path ? " --path '#{explicit_path}'" : " --path \"${TRY_PATH:-#{default_path}}\""
1301	      <<~SH
1302	        try() {
1303	          local out
1304	          out=$(/usr/bin/env ruby '#{script_path}' exec#{path_arg} "$@" 2>/dev/tty)
1305	          if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
1306	            eval "$out"
1307	          else
1308	            echo "$out"
1309	          fi
1310	        }
1311	      SH
1312	    end
1313	  end
1314	
1315	  def cmd_cd!(args, tries_path, and_type, and_exit, and_keys, and_confirm)
1316	    if args.first == "clone"
1317	      return cmd_clone!(args[1..-1] || [], tries_path)
1318	    end
1319	
1320	    # Support: try . [name] and try ./path [name]
1321	    if args.first && args.first.start_with?('.')
1322	      path_arg = args.shift
1323	      custom = args.join(' ')
1324	      repo_dir = File.expand_path(path_arg)
1325	      # Bare "try ." requires a name argument (too easy to invoke accidentally)
1326	      if path_arg == '.' && (custom.nil? || custom.strip.empty?)
1327	        STDERR.puts "Error: 'try .' requires a name argument"
1328	        STDERR.puts "Usage: try . <name>"
1329	        exit 1
1330	      end
1331	      base = if custom && !custom.strip.empty?
1332	        custom.gsub(/\s+/, '-')
1333	      else
1334	        File.basename(repo_dir)
1335	      end
1336	      date_prefix = Time.now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
1337	      base = resolve_unique_name_with_versioning(tries_path, date_prefix, base)
1338	      full_path = File.join(tries_path, "#{date_prefix}-#{base}")
1339	      # Use worktree if .git exists (file in worktrees, directory in regular repos)
1340	      if File.exist?(File.join(repo_dir, '.git'))
1341	        return script_worktree(full_path, repo_dir)
1342	      else
1343	        return script_mkdir_cd(full_path)
1344	      end
1345	    end
1346	
1347	    search_term = args.join(' ')
1348	
1349	    # Git URL shorthand → clone workflow
1350	    if is_git_uri?(search_term.split.first)
1351	      git_uri, custom_name = search_term.split(/\s+/, 2)
1352	      dir_name = generate_clone_directory_name(git_uri, custom_name)
1353	      unless dir_name
1354	        warn "Error: Unable to parse git URI: #{git_uri}"
1355	        exit 1
1356	      end
1357	      full_path = File.join(tries_path, dir_name)
1358	      return script_clone(full_path, git_uri)
1359	    end
1360	
1361	    # Regular interactive selector
1362	    selector = TrySelector.new(
1363	      search_term,
1364	      base_path: tries_path,
1365	      initial_input: and_type,
1366	      test_render_once: and_exit,
1367	      test_no_cls: (and_exit || (and_keys && !and_keys.empty?)),
1368	      test_keys: and_keys,
1369	      test_confirm: and_confirm
1370	    )
1371	    result = selector.run
1372	    return nil unless result
1373	
1374	    case result[:type]
1375	    when :delete
1376	      script_delete(result[:paths], result[:base_path])
1377	    when :mkdir
1378	      script_mkdir_cd(result[:path])
1379	    when :rename
1380	      script_rename(result[:base_path], result[:old], result[:new])
1381	    when :ascend
1382	      script_ascend(result[:source], result[:dest], result[:basename], result[:base_path])
1383	    else
1384	      script_cd(result[:path])
1385	    end
1386	  end

1388	  # --- Shell script helpers ---
1389	  SCRIPT_WARNING = "# if you can read this, you didn't launch try from an alias. run try --help."
1390	
1391	  def q(str)
1392	    "'" + str.gsub("'", %q('"'"')) + "'"
1393	  end
1394	
1395	  def emit_script(cmds)
1396	    puts SCRIPT_WARNING
1397	    cmds.each_with_index do |cmd, i|
1398	      if i == 0
1399	        print cmd
1400	      else
1401	        print "  #{cmd}"
1402	      end
1403	      if i < cmds.length - 1
1404	        puts " && \\"
1405	      else
1406	        puts
1407	      end
1408	    end
1409	  end
1410	
1411	  def script_cd(path)
1412	    ["touch #{q(path)}", "echo #{q(path)}", "cd #{q(path)}"]
1413	  end
1414	
1415	  def script_mkdir_cd(path)
1416	    ["mkdir -p #{q(path)}"] + script_cd(path)
1417	  end
1418	
1419	  def script_clone(path, uri)
1420	    ["mkdir -p #{q(path)}", "echo #{q("Using git clone to create this trial from #{uri}.")}", "git clone '#{uri}' #{q(path)}"] + script_cd(path)
1421	  end
1422	
1423	  def script_worktree(path, repo = nil)
1424	    r = repo ? q(repo) : nil
1425	    worktree_cmd = if r
1426	      "/usr/bin/env sh -c 'if git -C #{r} rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then repo=$(git -C #{r} rev-parse --show-toplevel); git -C \"$repo\" worktree add --detach #{q(path)} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi; exit 0'"
1427	    else
1428	      "/usr/bin/env sh -c 'if git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree >/dev/null 2>&1; then repo=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); git -C \"$repo\" worktree add --detach #{q(path)} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi; exit 0'"
1429	    end
1430	    src = repo || Dir.pwd
1431	    ["mkdir -p #{q(path)}", "echo #{q("Using git worktree to create this trial from #{src}.")}", worktree_cmd] + script_cd(path)
1432	  end
1433	
1434	  def script_delete(paths, base_path)
1435	    cmds = ["cd #{q(base_path)}"]
1436	    paths.each { |item| cmds << "test -d #{q(item[:basename])} && rm -rf #{q(item[:basename])}" }
1437	    cmds << "cd #{q(Dir.pwd)} 2>/dev/null || cd #{q(base_path)}"
1438	    cmds
1439	  end
1440	
1441	  def script_ascend(source, dest, basename, base_path)
1442	    symlink_path = File.join(base_path, basename)

1444	    git_file = File.join(source, '.git')

```text
1	# `try` in pwsh: bareword `try foo` won't parse, and try-cli's output errors with `The term '\' is not recognized`
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): you install `gem install try-cli` and add its shell integration, then in PowerShell `try foo` gives `The Try statement is missing its statement block`; or (once wrapped in a function) `try <name>` prints `The term '\' is not recognized as a name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or executable program`; the interactive selector never appears / renders into nowhere; `try init` claims to support pwsh but the resulting `try` command errors or does nothing; `& try foo` works but bareword `try foo` does not.
4	**First seen**: 2026-07 (porting tobi/try to this repo — `profile.d/32_try.ps1`)
5	**Affects**: PowerShell 7 on any OS; try-cli ≤ 1.9.3 (checked 1.7.1 installed + 1.9.3 source).
6	**Status**: worked around in `32_try.ps1` — bareword command renamed to **`tri`**; a native POSIX→pwsh translator replaces try's `eval`.
7	
8	## Symptom
9	
10	Two independent pwsh-specific breakages, one tool:
11	
12	```powershell
13	# 1) `try` is a reserved keyword (try/catch), so it can never be a bareword command:
14	try foo
15	# ParserError: The Try statement is missing its statement block.
16	
17	# 2) try-cli's runtime output is POSIX shell; Invoke-Expression chokes on it:
18	$out | Invoke-Expression
19	# The term '\' is not recognized as a name of a cmdlet, function, script file...
20	```
21	
22	try-cli 1.9.3 *detects* pwsh (`ENV["PSModulePath"]`) and emits a `function try { $out | Invoke-Expression }` wrapper — but (a) `try` can't be called bareword, and (b) the `$out` it evaluates is still POSIX.
23	
24	## Root cause
25	
26	**`try` is a PowerShell language keyword.** At statement position the parser lexes `try` as the start of a `try {} catch {}` block and demands a `{`. A function or alias named `try` is only reachable via the call operator (`& try …`), never as a bareword — this is a parse-time fact, unaffected by command resolution.
27	
28	**try-cli's runtime emitters are not shell-aware.** The Ruby `emit_script` / `script_*` helpers (`try.rb`) always print POSIX: commands joined by `` && \``+newline continuations, using `mkdir -p`, `touch`, `test -d`, `rm -rf`, `ln -s`, and `/usr/bin/env sh -c '…'`. pwsh's `Invoke-Expression` can't eval `` && \`` (backslash isn't a pwsh line-continuation — backtick is) or `mkdir -p` (pwsh `mkdir` has no `-p`). The pwsh `init` wrapper also redirects the selector TUI to a temp file (`2>$tempErr`), so the picker is invisible. In short: try-cli's pwsh support was never usable.
29	
30	## Workaround
31	
32	In `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/32_try.ps1`:
33	
34	1. **Name the command `tri`** (bareword-safe). Also define `function try { tri @args }` so `& try …` works for muscle memory.
35	2. **Don't use `try init`.** Run `ruby try.rb exec --path $env:TRY_PATH @args` directly, capture stdout, and **translate** its POSIX commands into native pwsh executed in the live session (`Set-Location`, `New-Item -ItemType Directory`, `git clone`, `git worktree add --detach`, …). Keep the child's stderr on the console so the selector TUI stays visible. Only translate a genuine emit-script (exit 0 + the `you didn't launch try from an alias` marker); print anything else (`Cancelled.`, errors) verbatim.
36	
37	```powershell
38	tri myproj              # create ~/src/tries/YYYY-MM-DD-myproj and cd in
39	tri https://github.com/user/repo   # clone into a dated dir and cd in
40	tri                     # fuzzy-select an existing trial
41	& try myproj            # the keyword-dodging alias, if you must type "try"
42	```
43	
44	## Prevention
45	
46	- **Never name a pwsh command after a keyword** (`try`, `if`, `for`, `switch`, `function`, `return`, `process`, `begin`, `end`, `data`, `filter`, `class`, `enum`, `hidden`, `trap`, …). Check with `[System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseInput('name foo',[ref]$null,[ref]$errs)`.
47	- **Assume a POSIX tool's shell integration is POSIX-only** until proven otherwise; a "supports pwsh" claim can mean "emits a pwsh wrapper" while the payload is still `sh`. Test `$out | Invoke-Expression` on real output before trusting it.
48	- The translator is coupled to try's emit format — `tests/Try.Tests.ps1` locks it down against hand-built goldens that mirror `emit_script`, and warns-and-continues on unknown verbs so a new try-cli version degrades to "still lands in the right dir" rather than crashing.
49	
50	## Related
51	
52	- `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/32_try.ps1` (the fix)
53	- `tests/Try.Tests.ps1`
54	- upstream: [tobi/try](https://github.com/tobi/try) `try.rb` (`emit_script`, `cmd_init!` pwsh branch)
55	- PowerShell: `about_Language_Keywords`, `about_Command_Precedence`
56

# Fix `tri` (try-cli) SIGWINCH crash on Windows + upstream PR

## Context

`tri` (the Ruby `try-cli` gem, v1.9.3, installed here via the `installTry` toggle and
driven by `profile.d/32_try.ps1`) crashes the moment its interactive picker opens:

\```
try.rb:80:in 'Signal.trap': unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)
    @old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
\```

**Root cause:** Windows Ruby (mingw/mswin) has no `SIGWINCH`. `try.rb` traps it
*unconditionally* in `TrySelector#setup_terminal`, so `Signal.trap('WINCH')` raises
`ArgumentError` and aborts before the main loop. `WINCH` is the **only** signal trapped
(no TSTP/CONT/INT), and the restore site (`try.rb:91`) is already nil-guarded
(`... if @old_winch_handler`, with `@old_winch_handler = nil` set at line 37), so a single
guard on line 80 fully fixes the crash without breaking teardown.

**Upstream:** `github.com/tobi/try` (Tobi Lütke), default branch `main`, active, README
claims Windows is in-scope, but **CI is Linux-only** (Ubuntu, Ruby 3.3, `rake`). No open
issue/PR addresses this crash — it's unclaimed. (PR #70 "Windows support" was closed
unmerged and explicitly punted on the Ruby version; PR #65 touched WINCH but for Unix
resize.) The gem is built from the single root `try.rb`; the C-port repo `tobi/try-cli` is
a decoy — **not** the target.

**Outcome:** `tri` works on this box immediately and stays working across `gem update` /
fresh machines, and the real fix lands upstream so `installTry` eventually needs no patch.

## The fix (one line, content-based)

In `try.rb`, guard the trap so it only runs where the signal exists:

\```ruby
# before
@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
# after
@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true } if Signal.list.key?('WINCH')
\```

`Signal.list.key?('WINCH')` is the idiomatic "trap only if supported" guard (portable, not
Windows-special-cased). Line 91 (restore) needs **no** change. Match on the substring, not a
line number, so it's robust to upstream drift.

> Caveat (not in scope for the crash fix): once the crash is gone, the picker's key-loop
> uses `IO.select([STDIN])` (L296), `STDIN.read_nonblock` (L307–308) and `STDIN.iflush`
> (L806), which can misbehave on the Windows console. We **verify the picker live** after
> patching; if it's broken, that's a separate follow-up, kept out of this focused PR to
> maximize merge odds (the maintainer has no Windows CI to validate a bigger change).

## Work items

### 1. Immediate local unblock (I do this)

- Write back as UTF-8 **no-BOM**, preserving existing EOLs (a BOM would corrupt the Ruby
  file) — same discipline as the earlier claude-hud `statusline.mjs` write.
- Note: reverted by a future `gem update try-cli` → that's what item 2 covers.

### 2. Durable self-healing patch in the chezmoi installer (I do this)
Add an idempotent post-`gem install` step to
`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl`, inside the existing
`{{ if .installTry -}}` block (after the `gem install try-cli` block, ~line 406):
- Resolve the installed `try.rb` via `ruby -e "...Gem::Specification.find_by_name('try-cli').gem_dir..."`
  (same lookup `32_try.ps1` already uses).
- If it contains the unguarded needle `Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }`
  **and** it is not already followed by `if Signal.list.key?`, append the guard; else no-op.
- Reuse the script's existing `Have` / `Info` / `Register-Failure` helpers; wrap in
  try/catch → never abort the apply (invariant #2). Write with `[System.IO.File]::WriteAllText`
  + UTF-8-no-BOM.
- Self-disables the day upstream ships a fixed release (needle gone). Known limit: a bare
  `gem update` that doesn't re-trigger this run_onchange won't re-patch — acceptable; the
  real fix is upstream and this covers fresh-machine + re-apply.

### 3. Upstream PR to `tobi/try` (I prepare; you run the `!` git/gh steps)
Per this repo's contribution model (identity `freyazh` ≠ owner → fork + PR; external
writes are handed off):
1. **You:** `!gh repo fork tobi/try --clone --fork-name try` into e.g. `C:\Code\tobi-try`

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Fix `tri` (try-cli) SIGWINCH crash on Windows + upstream PR

## Context

`tri` (the Ruby `try-cli` gem, v1.9.3, installed here via the `installTry` toggle and
driven by `profile.d/32_try.ps1`) crashes the moment its interactive picker opens:

```
try.rb:80:in 'Signal.trap': unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)
    @old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
```

**Root cause:** Windows Ruby (mingw/mswin) has no `SIGWINCH`. `try.rb` traps it
*unconditionally* in `TrySelector#setup_terminal`, so `Signal.trap('WINCH')` raises
`ArgumentError` and aborts before the main loop. `WINCH` is the **only** signal trapped
(no TSTP/CONT/INT), and the restore site (`try.rb:91`) is already nil-guarded
(`... if @old_winch_handler`, with `@old_winch_handler = nil` set at line 37), so a single
guard on line 80 fully fixes the crash without breaking teardown.

**Upstream:** `github.com/tobi/try` (Tobi Lütke), default branch `main`, active, README
claims Windows is in-scope, but **CI is Linux-only** (Ubuntu, Ruby 3.3, `rake`). No open
issue/PR addresses this crash — it's unclaimed. (PR #70 "Windows support" was closed
unmerged and explicitly punted on the Ruby version; PR #65 touched WINCH but for Unix
resize.) The gem is built from the single root `try.rb`; the C-port repo `tobi/try-cli` is
a decoy — **not** the target.

**Outcome:** `tri` works on this box immediately and stays working across `gem update` /
fresh machines, and the real fix lands upstream so `installTry` eventually needs no patch.

## The fix (one line, content-based)

In `try.rb`, guard the trap so it only runs where the signal exists:

```ruby
# before
@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
# after
@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true } if Signal.list.key?('WINCH')
```

`Signal.list.key?('WINCH')` is the idiomatic "trap only if supported" guard (portable, not
Windows-special-cased). Line 91 (restore) needs **no** change. Match on the substring, not a
line number, so it's robust to upstream drift.

> Caveat (not in scope for the crash fix): once the crash is gone, the picker's key-loop
> uses `IO.select([STDIN])` (L296), `STDIN.read_nonblock` (L307–308) and `STDIN.iflush`
> (L806), which can misbehave on the Windows console. We **verify the picker live** after
> patching; if it's broken, that's a separate follow-up, kept out of this focused PR to
> maximize merge odds (the maintainer has no Windows CI to validate a bigger change).

```md
# `tri` (try-cli) crashes on Windows: `unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)`

**Symptoms** (grep this section): running `tri` (bareword) — or any try-cli command that opens the interactive picker — dies immediately with `try.rb:80:in 'Signal.trap': unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)`; the traceback runs through `TrySelector#setup_terminal`, `TrySelector#run`, `Object#cmd_cd!`; the picker never draws. Verbatim:

\```
C:/Users/<you>/scoop/persist/ruby/gems/gems/try-cli-1.9.3/try.rb:80:in 'Signal.trap': unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)
    @old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
                                     ^^^^^^^
        from .../try.rb:80:in 'TrySelector#setup_terminal'
        from .../try.rb:46:in 'TrySelector#run'
        from .../try.rb:1371:in 'Object#cmd_cd!'
        from .../try.rb:1561:in '<main>'
\```

**First seen**: 2026-07 (try-cli 1.9.3 on this Windows box; `installTry` + `profile.d/32_try.ps1`)
**Affects**: try-cli ≤ 1.9.3 on Windows Ruby (`RUBY_PLATFORM` = `x64-mingw-ucrt` / any mingw/mswin). Not POSIX — macOS/Linux have `SIGWINCH`.
**Status**: worked around — live gem patched + self-healing installer step; fix submitted upstream to [tobi/try](https://github.com/tobi/try) (guard the trap).

## Symptom

`Signal.trap('WINCH')` raises `ArgumentError: unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH'` the instant the selector opens, aborting before the TUI renders. It fires from `TrySelector#setup_terminal` (`try.rb:80`), which `run` calls before the TTY check — so it crashes even when stdout/stderr are redirected.

## Root cause

Windows Ruby has **no `SIGWINCH`** (the SIGWINCH "window changed" signal is POSIX-only — it doesn't exist in the Windows signal set, so `Signal.list` has no `'WINCH'` key). try-cli traps it **unconditionally** to schedule a redraw on terminal resize:

\```ruby
# try.rb:80  (TrySelector#setup_terminal)
@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
\```

`WINCH` is the **only** signal try-cli traps (no TSTP/CONT/INT), and the restore site is already nil-guarded (`try.rb:91` `Signal.trap('WINCH', @old_winch_handler) if @old_winch_handler`, with `@old_winch_handler = nil` at `try.rb:37`). So a single guard on line 80 fixes the crash and the teardown chain still works (the guard leaves `@old_winch_handler` nil → line 91 no-ops).

**Secondary (not the crash, but next in line):** once past the trap, the picker's key-loop uses `IO.select([STDIN])`, `STDIN.read_nonblock`, `STDIN.iflush`, and `IO.console.winsize` — all POSIX-console assumptions. `winsize` in particular raises `Errno::EBADF - Bad file descriptor` when stderr is **not** a real Windows console (redirected to a file/pipe, or a mintty/MSYS pty). In normal `tri` use this is fine: `32_try.ps1` keeps the child's stderr on the pwsh **console**, where `winsize` works. Only surfaces under redirection or non-conhost terminals; kept out of the crash fix.

## Workaround

Guard the trap so it only runs where the signal exists (portable, not Windows-special-cased):

\```ruby
@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true } if Signal.list.key?('WINCH')
\```

Applied in three places:

1. **Live gem** — the same one-liner edited into the installed `try.rb` for immediate relief. Reverted by a future `gem update try-cli`.
2. **Durable / self-healing** — `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` (inside `{{ "{{ if .installTry }}" }}`) resolves the installed `try.rb` and appends the guard **idempotently** after `gem install try-cli` (no-ops once guarded or once upstream drops the raw trap). Survives fresh machines / re-apply.
3. **Upstream** — PR to [tobi/try](https://github.com/tobi/try) (`main`) so a future release needs no local patch.

## Prevention

- **Guard every signal trap that isn't universal.** Only `INT`/`TERM` are safe cross-platform; `WINCH`/`TSTP`/`CONT` are POSIX-only. Wrap with `Signal.trap(sig, &blk) if Signal.list.key?(sig)`, or check `Gem.win_platform?`. `Signal.list` is the authoritative per-platform set.
- **A "works on any system with Ruby" tool can still assume a POSIX TTY** in its input loop (`IO.select`/`read_nonblock`/`iflush`/`winsize`). On Windows they work only against a real conhost console — verify in `pwsh`/Windows Terminal, not under redirected streams or mintty.

## Related

- `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/32_try.ps1` — the `tri` command that shells out to `try.rb exec`
- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` — the idempotent guard step
- sibling pitfall: [`try-cli-pwsh-support-emits-posix.md`](try-cli-pwsh-support-emits-posix.md) — try-cli's other pwsh breakage (bareword keyword + POSIX emit)
- upstream: [tobi/try](https://github.com/tobi/try) `try.rb` (`TrySelector#setup_terminal`, lines 80/91)

**How to apply:** write files as LF and stage directly — no CRLF conversion step. Only if `git add` complains `LF would be replaced by CRLF` on some specific path should you check that path's own `git ls-files --eol`/`git check-attr -a` and match it. Don't blanket-normalize to CRLF. Related: [[agent-write-guardrails]].

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```md
## Problem

On Windows, `try` crashes the instant the interactive picker opens:

\```
try.rb:80:in 'Signal.trap': unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)
    @old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
\```

`SIGWINCH` is POSIX-only — it isn't in the Windows signal set, so `Signal.list`
has no `'WINCH'` key and `Signal.trap('WINCH')` raises `ArgumentError`.
`TrySelector#setup_terminal` traps it unconditionally, so the process dies before
the TUI renders. This hits any Windows Ruby (`RUBY_PLATFORM` = `x64-mingw-ucrt` /
mingw / mswin). The README says try "works on any system with Ruby" and the gem
declares no platform restriction, so Windows is in scope.

## Fix

Trap `WINCH` only where the platform actually has it:

\```ruby
@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true } if Signal.list.key?('WINCH')
\```

`WINCH` is the only signal `try` traps, and the restore site in
`restore_terminal` is already nil-guarded
(`Signal.trap('WINCH', @old_winch_handler) if @old_winch_handler`, with
`@old_winch_handler = nil` set in `initialize`). On Windows the guard leaves
`@old_winch_handler` nil, so teardown is a clean no-op and nothing regresses. On
POSIX, `Signal.list.key?('WINCH')` is true and behaviour is unchanged — no loss,
including live-resize redraw. Using `Signal.list.key?('WINCH')` rather than
`Gem.win_platform?` keeps it a portable "trap only if the signal exists" check.

## Scope / testing

Deliberately minimal — just the crash. Verified on `x64-mingw-ucrt` Ruby that
`Signal.list.key?('WINCH')` is `false` and the picker now reaches
`setup_terminal` without raising. CI here is Linux-only (where `WINCH` exists),
so this path can't be exercised there; the guard is a no-op on the tested
platforms.

Follow-up (intentionally **not** in this PR): once the crash is gone, the
picker's input loop still assumes a POSIX console — `IO.select([STDIN])`,
`STDIN.read_nonblock`, `STDIN.iflush`, and `IO.console.winsize` (which raises
`Errno::EBADF` when stderr isn't a real console). Making the interactive picker
fully functional on Windows is separate work; PR #70's "full parity" attempt
took a non-Ruby route and was closed. Keeping this to the one-line crash guard so
it's easy to accept.

```text
1	# Repository Guidelines
2	
3	## Project Structure & Module Organization
4	- `try.rb`: Single-file Ruby CLI and TUI (no gems).
5	- `flake.nix`/`flake.lock`: Nix packaging and Home Manager module.
6	- `README.md`: Usage, installation, and philosophy.
7	- Tries live outside this repo (default `~/src/tries`, configurable via `TRY_PATH`).
8	
9	## CLI Interface
10	- `try init [PATH]`: Emits a tiny shell wrapper function for your shell. PATH sets the root (absolute path recommended). The function evals the printed, shell-neutral script to `cd` into selections.
11	- `try cd [QUERY]`: Launches the interactive selector. If `QUERY` looks like a Git URL, it performs a clone workflow instead. Prints a shell script to stdout; use via the installed function.
12	- `try . [name]`: Shorthand to create a date-prefixed directory and, if inside a Git repo, add a detached worktree. Optional `name` overrides the basename.
13	- `try worktree dir [name]`: Same as above but explicit CLI, useful without the shell wrapper.
14	- `try clone <git-uri> [name]`: Clones into the root. Default name is `YYYY-MM-DD-user-repo` (strips `.git`). Optional `name` overrides.
15	- Flags: `--path PATH` (for `cd`/`clone`) overrides the root for that call; `--help` prints global help.
16	- Environment: `TRY_PATH` sets the default root when not using `--path`. `TRY_PROJECTS` sets the graduate destination (default: parent of `TRY_PATH`).
17	- UI keys: `↑/↓` or `Ctrl-P/N` navigate, `Enter` select, `Backspace` delete char, `Ctrl-D` delete dir (requires typing `YES`), `Ctrl-G` graduate (promote try to project), `Ctrl-R` rename, `ESC` cancel.
18	
19	### Shorthands and Worktrees
20	- `try .`: Creates a new date-prefixed directory using the current working directory’s basename. If inside a Git repo, a detached worktree is added; otherwise this is a plain directory.
21	
22	### Shell behavior
23	- Emitted commands use absolute, quoted paths and are shell-neutral (bash/zsh/fish). Only the wrapper function generated by `init` differs per shell.
24	
25	## Build, Test, and Development Commands
26	- `nix run`: Run the packaged CLI (e.g., `nix run . -- --help`).
27	- `nix build`: Build the binary derivation; output at `./result/bin/try`.
28	- `./try.rb init ~/src/tries`: Emit shell function for your shell config.
29	- `./try.rb cd`: Launch interactive selector; prints `cd` script to stdout.
30	- `./try.rb clone <git-uri> [name]`: Clone into date-prefixed directory.
31	
32	## Coding Style & Naming Conventions
33	- Ruby, 2-space indent, standard library only; keep it single-file unless necessary.
34	- Prefer small, pure functions; no global state beyond `ENV` reads.
35	- UI tokens live in `UI::TOKEN_MAP`; add tokens with clear names. UI printing runs through `UI.expand_tokens`.
36	- Shell emission goes through `UI.emit_tasks_script` (don’t handcraft `$dir` scripts).
37	- Directory names: `YYYY-MM-DD-name` (auto-generated); keep lowercase/kebab-case.
38	- Nix: keep `packages.default` minimal; avoid extra build inputs.
39	
40	## Spec System
41	- `spec/`: Contains markdown specifications and automated tests.
42	- `spec/*.md`: Human-readable specs defining expected behavior (e.g., `init_spec.md`, `tui_spec.md`, `fuzzy_matching.md`).
43	- `spec/tests/`: Shell-based test suite that validates implementations against specs.
44	- `spec/tests/runner.sh`: Test runner that executes all `test_*.sh` files against any `try` binary.
45	- Run tests: `./spec/tests/runner.sh /path/to/try` (supports wrappers like valgrind).
46	
47	**Important**: Specs must reflect the full feature set of `try`. They serve as the canonical reference for behavior, enabling new implementations (in any language) to be validated against the same test suite. When adding or changing features, update both the relevant spec markdown and add corresponding tests.
48	
49	## Testing Guidelines
50	- Primary testing is via the spec system: `./spec/tests/runner.sh ./try.rb`
51	- Manual flows for exploratory testing:
52	  - `TRY_PATH=$(mktemp -d) ./try.rb cd` then create/select directories.
53	  - Validate delete confirmation and scoring by changing `mtime`/`ctime`.
54	  - Test clone paths: `./try.rb clone https://github.com/user/repo.git`.
55	- If adding logic, add tests to the spec system under `spec/tests/`.
56	- Prefer testing the printed shell via regex matches. When adding tokens, add simple tests to validate token expansion and non-TTY flush behavior.
57	
58	## Version Bumps
59	When bumping the version, update **all three** locations and tag:
60	1. `try.rb`: `VERSION = "X.Y.Z"` constant.
61	2. `VERSION`: Plain-text file in repo root (single line).
62	3. `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z` after committing.
63	
64	## Commit & Pull Request Guidelines
65	- Commits: short, imperative subject; optional scope. Examples:
66	  - `fix: reset token clears colors`
67	  - `ui: improve selected row highlight`
68	  - `nix: wire Home Manager module`
69	- PRs: include a clear description, before/after terminal screenshot or asciinema for UI changes, linked issues, and notes on behavior or config (`TRY_PATH`). Update `README.md` when flags, defaults, or UX change.
70	
71	## Security & Configuration Tips
72	- `TRY_PATH` controls the workspace root; avoid pointing at sensitive paths.
73	- Destructive action (delete) requires typing `YES`; keep this safeguard.
74	- `clone` shells out to `git`; it writes only under `TRY_PATH`.
75	
76	## Directory Scoring Algorithm
77	- Date prefix bonus: Names starting with `YYYY-MM-DD-` get a base `+2.0`.
78	- Fuzzy match (when searching):
79	  - Match is subsequence-based, per-char `+1.0`.
80	  - Word-boundary bonus `+1.0` when a match starts at index 0 or after non-word.
81	  - Proximity bonus `+1/√(gap+1)` for consecutive matches.
82	  - If not all query chars match, score is `0`.
83	  - Density bonus multiplies by `len(query)/(last_match_index+1)`.
84	  - Length penalty multiplies by `10/(len(name)+10)` to prefer shorter names.
85	- Time-based bonuses (always applied):
86	  - Creation time: `+ 2/√(days_since_created+1)`.
87	  - Last modified/accessed: `+ 3/√(hours_since_access+1)`.
88	- Sorting: When no query, items are ordered by the time/date-influenced score; with a query, only matches with positive score appear, sorted descending.
89
```

Actually, I need to think through this more carefully — `module_function` creates both a singleton method on the Signal module's singleton class AND a private instance method. When I define a new singleton method with the same name, it overwrites that slot entirely. Then when I call `remove_method` to delete my override, it's gone, but the original `module_function` definition is also gone since there's only one method slot. So I'd need a different approach to temporarily shadow it without losing the original.

The better strategy is to save the original Method object before overriding it, then restore it afterward. I can grab the bound Method with `Signal.method(:list)`, define my override, and then use `define_singleton_method` with that saved Method object to restore the original behavior — `define_singleton_method` accepts a Method object as the body, so passing the original Method back will re-establish the original functionality.

<tool-use data-tool-type="write" data-tool-name="Write"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```txt
fix: guard SIGWINCH trap so Windows Ruby doesn't crash

TrySelector#setup_terminal trapped SIGWINCH unconditionally. On Windows
Ruby (x64-mingw-ucrt) SIGWINCH isn't a supported signal, so
Signal.trap('WINCH') raises `ArgumentError: unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH'`
the instant the picker opens, aborting before the TUI renders.

Trap it only when the platform has it (`Signal.list.key?('WINCH')`). WINCH
is the only signal trapped and restore_terminal is already nil-guarded, so
teardown is unaffected; POSIX behaviour (including live-resize redraw) is
unchanged. Adds a Minitest that stubs Signal.list to assert setup_terminal
doesn't raise when WINCH is absent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

```

```text
1	# `tri` (try-cli) crashes on Windows: `unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)`
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section): running `tri` (bareword) — or any try-cli command that opens the interactive picker — dies immediately with `try.rb:80:in 'Signal.trap': unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)`; the traceback runs through `TrySelector#setup_terminal`, `TrySelector#run`, `Object#cmd_cd!`; the picker never draws. Verbatim:
4	
5	```
6	C:/Users/<you>/scoop/persist/ruby/gems/gems/try-cli-1.9.3/try.rb:80:in 'Signal.trap': unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)
7	    @old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
8	                                     ^^^^^^^
9	        from .../try.rb:80:in 'TrySelector#setup_terminal'
10	        from .../try.rb:46:in 'TrySelector#run'
11	        from .../try.rb:1371:in 'Object#cmd_cd!'
12	        from .../try.rb:1561:in '<main>'
13	```
14	
15	**First seen**: 2026-07 (try-cli 1.9.3 on this Windows box; `installTry` + `profile.d/32_try.ps1`)
16	**Affects**: try-cli ≤ 1.9.3 on Windows Ruby (`RUBY_PLATFORM` = `x64-mingw-ucrt` / any mingw/mswin). Not POSIX — macOS/Linux have `SIGWINCH`.
17	**Status**: worked around — live gem patched + self-healing installer step; fix submitted upstream to [tobi/try](https://github.com/tobi/try) (guard the trap).
18	
19	## Symptom
20	
21	`Signal.trap('WINCH')` raises `ArgumentError: unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH'` the instant the selector opens, aborting before the TUI renders. It fires from `TrySelector#setup_terminal` (`try.rb:80`), which `run` calls before the TTY check — so it crashes even when stdout/stderr are redirected.
22	
23	## Root cause
24	
25	Windows Ruby has **no `SIGWINCH`** (the SIGWINCH "window changed" signal is POSIX-only — it doesn't exist in the Windows signal set, so `Signal.list` has no `'WINCH'` key). try-cli traps it **unconditionally** to schedule a redraw on terminal resize:
26	
27	```ruby
28	# try.rb:80  (TrySelector#setup_terminal)
29	@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true }
30	```
31	
32	`WINCH` is the **only** signal try-cli traps (no TSTP/CONT/INT), and the restore site is already nil-guarded (`try.rb:91` `Signal.trap('WINCH', @old_winch_handler) if @old_winch_handler`, with `@old_winch_handler = nil` at `try.rb:37`). So a single guard on line 80 fixes the crash and the teardown chain still works (the guard leaves `@old_winch_handler` nil → line 91 no-ops).
33	
34	**Secondary (not the crash, but next in line):** once past the trap, the picker's key-loop uses `IO.select([STDIN])`, `STDIN.read_nonblock`, `STDIN.iflush`, and `IO.console.winsize` — all POSIX-console assumptions. `winsize` in particular raises `Errno::EBADF - Bad file descriptor` when stderr is **not** a real Windows console (redirected to a file/pipe, or a mintty/MSYS pty). In normal `tri` use this is fine: `32_try.ps1` keeps the child's stderr on the pwsh **console**, where `winsize` works. Only surfaces under redirection or non-conhost terminals; kept out of the crash fix.
35	
36	## Workaround
37	
38	Guard the trap so it only runs where the signal exists (portable, not Windows-special-cased):
39	
40	```ruby
41	@old_winch_handler = Signal.trap('WINCH') { @needs_redraw = true } if Signal.list.key?('WINCH')
42	```
43	
44	Applied in three places:
45	
46	1. **Live gem** — the same one-liner edited into the installed `try.rb` for immediate relief. Reverted by a future `gem update try-cli`.
47	2. **Durable / self-healing** — `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` (inside `{{ "{{ if .installTry }}" }}`) resolves the installed `try.rb` and appends the guard **idempotently** after `gem install try-cli` (no-ops once guarded or once upstream drops the raw trap). Survives fresh machines / re-apply.
48	3. **Upstream** — PR to [tobi/try](https://github.com/tobi/try) (`main`) so a future release needs no local patch.
49	
50	## Prevention
51	
52	- **Guard every signal trap that isn't universal.** Only `INT`/`TERM` are safe cross-platform; `WINCH`/`TSTP`/`CONT` are POSIX-only. Wrap with `Signal.trap(sig, &blk) if Signal.list.key?(sig)`, or check `Gem.win_platform?`. `Signal.list` is the authoritative per-platform set.
53	- **A "works on any system with Ruby" tool can still assume a POSIX TTY** in its input loop (`IO.select`/`read_nonblock`/`iflush`/`winsize`). On Windows they work only against a real conhost console — verify in `pwsh`/Windows Terminal, not under redirected streams or mintty.
54	
55	## Related
56	
57	- `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/32_try.ps1` — the `tri` command that shells out to `try.rb exec`
58	- `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` — the idempotent guard step
59	- sibling pitfall: [`try-cli-pwsh-support-emits-posix.md`](try-cli-pwsh-support-emits-posix.md) — try-cli's other pwsh breakage (bareword keyword + POSIX emit)
60	- upstream: [tobi/try](https://github.com/tobi/try) `try.rb` (`TrySelector#setup_terminal`, lines 80/91)

```md
# try-cli (`tri`) interactive picker hangs on Windows

**Status**: P? — deferred; needs a spike (is the full raw TUI viable on the Windows console, or input-only?)
**Effort**: L
**Related**: `pitfalls/try-cli-sigwinch-crash-windows.md` · `dot_config/powershell/profile.d/32_try.ps1` · `.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl` · upstream [tobi/try PR #123](https://github.com/tobi/try/pull/123) (crash fix) · [PR #70](https://github.com/tobi/try/pull/70) (closed Windows attempt)

## Context

2026-07. The SIGWINCH **crash** (`unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH'`) is fixed — one-line
guard shipped as [tobi/try PR #123](https://github.com/tobi/try/pull/123), plus a local
live-gem patch + self-healing installer step (see the pitfall doc). But that only stops the
crash: **bare `tri` (the interactive fuzzy picker) now hangs** instead. `Ctrl-C` exits;
`tri <name>` (create-a-dated-dir path) is usable. So `tri` is crash-free but the picker is
unusable on Windows.

Deferred per maintainer: not worth the Windows-TUI rabbit hole right now — document + track,
and cross-reference the upstream context in the dotfiles-windows PR instead.

## Root cause

The selector's key loop assumes a POSIX console. In `try.rb` (1.9.3):

\```ruby
# try.rb ~290  TrySelector#read_key
loop do
  ...
  ready = IO.select([STDIN], nil, nil, 0.1)   # line 296 — never signals on Windows console
  return read_keypress if ready
end
# read_keypress: STDIN.getc + STDIN.read_nonblock(3/2)  (lines 302, 307-308)
\```

`IO.select` on Windows only works on **sockets**, not console/pipe handles — so `ready`
never becomes truthy and the loop spins forever without ever reading a key → hang.
Companion POSIX-console assumptions in the same area:

- `STDIN.read_nonblock` (`try.rb:307-308`) — not truly non-blocking on the Windows console.
- `STDIN.iflush` (`try.rb:806`, cooked-mode rename/confirm) — POSIX TCFLUSH ioctl; may raise `NotImplementedError`.
- `IO.console.winsize` (`lib/tui.rb:323`, `Tui::Terminal.size`) — raises `Errno::EBADF` when the stream isn't a real conhost console (redirected, or mintty/MSYS pty). `Tui::Terminal.size` rescues `IOError, Errno::ENOTTY, Errno::EOPNOTSUPP, Errno::ENODEV` but **not** `Errno::EBADF`.

## Approach (candidate, unverified)

1. **Input loop** — on `Gem.win_platform?`, replace the `IO.select` poll in `read_key` with a
   blocking single-char read via `STDIN.getch` (from `io/console`, which *does* work on the
   Windows console). Drop the resize poll — there's no `SIGWINCH` on Windows anyway.
2. **Special keys** — the Windows console delivers arrows/function keys as a `\xE0` (or `\x00`)
   prefix + scancode, **not** the POSIX `ESC[` sequences `read_keypress` expects. Add a
   Windows scancode → internal-key map (UP/DOWN/etc.) so navigation works.
3. **winsize** — add `Errno::EBADF` to the `Tui::Terminal.size` rescue so a non-conhost stream
   degrades to the 24×80 fallback instead of erroring.

## Open questions (the spike)

- Does conhost / Windows Terminal / WezTerm handle raw-mode + alt-screen + ANSI well enough for
  the full picker TUI, or is this a larger rewrite than just the input loop?
- Does `io/console` `raw`/`getch` behave under the pwsh `& ruby try.rb exec …` invocation
  (`32_try.ps1` keeps the child's stderr on the console)?
- Test across conhost vs Windows Terminal vs WezTerm — behavior differs.

## Testing constraint

try-cli's test-key mode (`--and-keys`) **bypasses `read_key` entirely** (returns injected
keys before reaching `IO.select`), so the Windows input path **cannot be unit-tested
headlessly**. Requires a manual terminal loop: patch → run `tri` in the terminal → iterate.

## Upstream / distribution decision

- tobi **closed** the big Windows PR [#70](https://github.com/tobi/try/pull/70)
  ("full parity") — it took a separate-scripts (non-Ruby) route and admitted the Ruby version
  has Windows issues. So a picker-input PR to `tobi/try` has **low merge odds**.
- Likely keep any picker fix as a **local self-healing installer patch** (like the SIGWINCH
  guard) rather than an upstream PR — unless the maintainer signals renewed interest in the
  Ruby Windows path.

## Revisit criteria

- We actually want the fuzzy picker on Windows (vs. living with `tri <name>` + Ctrl-C).
- Upstream reopens Ruby Windows support, or PR #123 gets a warm reception worth extending.

## References

- pitfall: `pitfalls/try-cli-sigwinch-crash-windows.md`
- crash-fix PR (ours): https://github.com/tobi/try/pull/123
- closed Windows PR: https://github.com/tobi/try/pull/70
- `try.rb` read_key / read_keypress: https://github.com/tobi/try/blob/main/try.rb

```md
## What

`tri` (the `try-cli` gem installed via `installTry`) crashes on Windows the instant its
picker opens:

\```
try.rb:80: Signal.trap('WINCH'): unsupported signal 'SIGWINCH' (ArgumentError)
\```

`SIGWINCH` is POSIX-only; `try.rb` traps it unconditionally in `TrySelector#setup_terminal`.
This PR makes `tri` crash-free on Windows.

## Changes

- **`.chezmoiscripts/run_onchange_after_10_packages.ps1.tmpl`** — idempotent post-`gem install`
  step that appends `if Signal.list.key?('WINCH')` to the installed `try.rb`. Self-healing:
  no-ops once the guard is present or once upstream ships a fix. Fault-tolerant (wrapped,
  `Register-Failure`, never aborts the apply).
- **`pitfalls/try-cli-sigwinch-crash-windows.md`** — symptom-first record; also indexes the
  previously-unlisted `try-cli-pwsh-support-emits-posix` sibling.
- **`TODO.md` + `backlog/try-cli-windows-picker-input-loop.md`** — the deferred follow-up (below).

## Upstream

- The real fix is a one-line guard submitted upstream: **tobi/try#123**
  (`Signal.trap('WINCH') { … } if Signal.list.key?('WINCH')` + a Minitest). Once released,
  `gem install try-cli` gets it and the installer step becomes a no-op.
- Context: tobi/try's earlier Windows PR **#70** was closed unmerged (it took a non-Ruby route
  and admitted the Ruby version has Windows issues), so this repo carries a local self-healing
  patch rather than depending on upstream timing.

## Known limitation (deferred)

The crash is fixed, but bare `tri` (the interactive picker) then **hangs** on the Windows
console — its `read_key` loop uses `IO.select([STDIN])`, which only works on sockets there
(`Ctrl-C` exits; `tri <name>` create works). That's a separate Windows-console input port,
tracked in `backlog/try-cli-windows-picker-input-loop.md` and `TODO.md` (`[?/L]`), not
attempted here.

## Validation

- Live gem patched + verified: `Signal.list.key?('WINCH')` is `false` on `x64-mingw-ucrt`; the
  picker reaches `setup_terminal` with no `ArgumentError`.
- Rendered template AST-parses; the patch predicate is unit-tested (idempotent on
  already-guarded / upstream-`unless` inputs).

```
